newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALPINE SKIING-ORTLIEB FASTEST IN DOWNHILL PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ORTLIEB FASTEST IN DOWNHILL PRACTICE.

text.p: Austrians issued a warning to Frenchman Luc Alphand when they snatched the six fastest times of the first training for the first downhill of the men's World Cup season on Thursday.
World champion Patrick Ortlieb was fastest in 1:52.52 ahead of compatriots Joseph Strobl, the 1994 winner here, Werner Franz, Fritz Strobl, Guenther Mader and Roland Assinger.
Alphand, the World Cup downhill holder, was seventh on 1:54.23.
"I feel the pressure mounting", said Alphand, who last year became the first Frenchman to win a World Cup downhill in the country's most famous ski resort.
"Winning here last year was by far the most moving moment of last season but it will be dificult to repeat. It has snowed a lot here lately which is good for tourists, not for skiers," he added.
The snow did not seem to disturb Ortlieb, who said he was all out to upstage Alphand after his fine run on the OK piste.
"I've won on the other side of the mountain," said the Austrian, who was Olympic champion here in 1992 on the Bellevarde piste. "Now I want to win on this side.
"I have been world champion and Olympic champion. My goal this season is to take the World Cup away from Alphand," he added.
